column1: # lore-claims.tsv — every system the saga and the lore name, with the door that should keep it (plan 350 part A).
# One row per claim, tab-separated: system · claim (the saga's words, short) · door (a path in this tree; "-" for none)
# · command (read-only, run from the tree root with a timeout) · expect ("rc0", or an extended regex the output must
# match) · state ("planned" when the house itself records the system as not yet built; else empty).
# Measured by bin/records/lore-audit.sh. A missing door is FALSE, a door whose command does not bear the claim
# out is PARTIAL, a command that bears it out is TRUE. Nothing here names a machine, a person or a path in a home.

column2: the gateway every crossing passes over
writes the words (a specialist of the house)
the room that spans houses, where different owners meet
the workers, each in a sealed sandbox, each on its own branch
judges and reviews every PR
keeps the house's rules and its craft
the tunnel that carries a signal out, never to a hall
the room where every agent on every machine and the Allfather speak
the session lock: one hand holds the reins
the skill forge: a new skill made, tested inside Utgard, written to the well
refines a finished run into a sharper skill
signs every agent's rune of introduction; nothing crosses unvouched
column4: grep -l -e 'rune of introduction' -e 'agent identity' bin/agents/*.sh 2>/dev/null | head -2

researches and flies out each day to see
the one road every system takes when it has something to say
scouts the ground before anyone builds
takes the broad slice, many files at once
the well: recalled before work, written after it
